items.value:
Review comments and decisions must survive browser reloads without moving
plan authority away from the source file.

Add a local review service, a durable event table, and one operator-facing
review queue.

Land persistence first, expose narrow service contracts, then enable the
review workspace behind a rollout flag.

entries.gist: Define snapshots, outcomes, and review locations
Settle ownership, storage, and rollout boundaries
Show the service flow and planned file changes
Review code, data, table, HTTP, GraphQL, and gRPC contracts
Preview the queue used to resolve review threads

children.value: Verify the causal boundary, the in-place lens, and the historical state.

Approve the persistence boundary and staged rollout before implementation
begins. The browser remains a review surface; the MDX plan on disk remains
authoritative.

The first release runs locally, but the storage boundary should admit shared
review later.
The service stores feedback and decisions, never a competing copy of the plan.
A later shared service can retain the same repository interface.

options.title: Review service repository
options.summary: Keep persistence behind the service contract.

children.value: The service stores feedback and decisions, never a competing copy of the plan.
A later shared service can retain the same repository interface.

options.title: Plan-adjacent files on disk
options.summary: Write review events beside the plan under a dot directory.

children.value:
Review records sit next to the plan without competing with it, and a reviewer
can inspect them with ordinary file tools.

A shared service would have to import loose per-plan files and invent the
ordering guarantees the format never enforced.

model.question: Ship the workspace behind a local feature flag?

options.title: Yes
options.summary: Lets maintainers exercise the full review loop before it becomes the default.

options.title: No
options.summary: Reduces rollout code but exposes every local user at once.

model.question: Which event store should back the first release?

children.value: The store must preserve thread order, anchor updates, and crash-safe writes.
A thread event and its latest anchor must commit together.
Contributors should not need a separately managed database service.

options.title: SQLite
options.summary: Use one embedded database owned by the review service.

children.value: Transactions cover the event and anchor rows in one file.
The service opens the database directly.

options.title: PostgreSQL
options.summary: Run the same server store planned for shared review.

children.value: Relational transactions provide the required boundary.
Every contributor must start and maintain a database server.

The repository seam contains the code change, but persisted local data still
needs a migration.

footer.value: One source file, one feedback stream, and two coordinated readers.

model.source:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Reviewer
  participant Doc as Review document
  participant Service as Local review service
  participant Store as Event store
  participant Agent as Authoring agent
  participant Plan as Plan source

  Reviewer->>Doc: Select a block and write feedback
  Doc->>Service: Append comment with its anchor
  Service->>Store: Persist event and premise snapshot
  Service-->>Doc: Thread id and sequence
  Service->>Agent: Deliver the pending request

  Agent->>Service: Claim the request
  Service->>Store: Freeze the baseline snapshot
  Agent->>Plan: Read the current source

  alt Outcome is changed
    Agent->>Plan: Revise the plan source
    Agent->>Service: Respond with changed block ids
    Service->>Store: Record the result snapshot
    Service-->>Doc: Was and Now diff for this feedback
  else Answered, declined, or needs input
    Agent->>Service: Respond without editing
    Service-->>Doc: Answer with no diff
  end

  Reviewer->>Doc: Resolve the thread or reply again
  Reviewer->>Service: Accept the plan
